name: 3I/ATLAS
periodText: At least about 1 hour; not determined
credit: Hui, Jewitt, Mutchler, Agarwal and Kim (2026), ApJL, Hubble WFC3 nucleus photometry (arXiv:2601.21569)
shapeMeaning: Hubble photometry gives an effective radius of 1.3 ± 0.2 km, assuming V-band geometric albedo 0.04, and brightness changes of at least 0.8 mag imply a sky-plane axis ratio of 2:1 or more. No shape model, pole or period was published. This display is a prolate ellipsoid at exactly the minimum 2:1 ratio, sized so the geometric mean of its largest and smallest cross-sections equals π × (1.3 km)²: full axes 4.37 × 2.19 × 2.19 km. A longer body, another albedo or a different shape would change it.
orientationMeaning: Arbitrary display pole and meridian. No rotation pole or phase has been measured.
introduction: The third known interstellar visitor passed the Sun in October 2025. Hubble later picked out its nucleus from the surrounding dust; this view shows an elongated shape of that measured brightness, not a resolved image.
card: The third interstellar object seen passing through the Solar System.
datasetSummary: An elongated body sized from Hubble brightness with an assumed dark surface; the true shape is unknown.
survey: Included: Hui et al. (2026) Hubble WFC3 photometry, December 2025 to January 2026: effective radius 1.3 ± 0.2 km at pV 0.04 and axis ratio at least 2:1.
Superseded for size: Jewitt et al. (2025) July 2025 Hubble images, which limited the radius to at most 2.8 km while dust hid the nucleus.
Excluded: artist impressions and coma photographs as surface textures; the nucleus is unresolved.
Included: JPL Horizons 2026-09-03 heliocentric osculating trajectory and independent vectors; not a simulation of its non-gravitational acceleration.
